first.rationale: The two declining metrics this quarter (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) map directly onto the mechanism described in memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifts first-week activation). That is the only candidate that addresses both symptoms with a single lever, and both prior results are described as durable rather than borrowed-from-the-future. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor, but memory_73 is explicit that it bought acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and should not be generalized; under a sustainable long-term qualified-revenue objective that is a value-destroying trade, and competitive pressure does not change the retention mechanism. Referral incentives (memory_57) are clean but act on established customers and do nothing for the two metrics that actually moved. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a real result but addresses a segment that is not the source of the decline. I am spending both verification pulls on the memories I am actually leaning on rather than on the one I am declining, because a wrong belief in memory_86/memory_31 would misdirect the whole slot, whereas memory_73 only needs to be roughly right to justify a no. What I want from the archive: the segment the original onboarding and signup tests ran on, whether the lift was measured on activation itself or on a proxy, and how long the durability window actually was. Downstream risk I am flagging rather than ignoring: cutting required fields removes data that later stages consume. Fewer qualifying fields can degrade lead routing and firmographic scoring, which is precisely the channel by which enterprise prospects get pushed into the demo-request path that memory_44 says outperforms. So a naive field cut could lift a headline activation number while quietly reducing qualified pipeline, which is the metric I am actually optimizing. Guard: scope the test to self-serve SMB, keep the routing-relevant fields, and instrument downstream qualified-pipeline quality alongside activation rather than reading activation alone. Standard experiment scale with a holdout, not a broad rollout, since the inherited results are older than the current regime and the competitor shift may have changed who is signing up.
